analysis:
The supplied units are the BASE text of docs/architecture/inference.md, covering lines 1-797 and a Nemotron Super slot description. The PR changes only documentation. The patch excerpt shows two hunks. The first, at head lines ~404-413, adds a description of releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad: eviction and pre-accept release retained free KV segments and drop MLX's buffer cache once before judging load room. The second, at head lines ~1053-1073, describes segmented paged admission parking free 64 MiB segments per pool, up to min(2 GiB, slot grant/8), outside the grant, floor and ledger charge. The excerpt is truncated, so the rest of that second hunk (zero-fill wording) was not visible.

Security relevance: the parked segments are described as outside the ledger charge. If those segments are reinstalled for a different request or tenant without zeroing, that would bear on T-028 (residual GPU/KV data) and on cross-tenant isolation. The visible text says new segments wrap zero-fil..., which suggests zero-filling, but the text is cut off. I cannot confirm from this evidence that reused parked segments are zeroed or scoped, or that the parked memory is accounted for in the shared budget (an availability concern). This is a documentation change describing code that is not supplied, so it is not a verified regression.

No code, authorization, attestation, encryption or billing changes are visible. The existing prefix-cache and SSD tier threat (T-041) is not altered by the visible text. No findings. The next pass should check the actual implementation of segment parking and reinstall for zeroization on reuse (T-028), and whether parked-but-uncharged memory can starve admission or be attributed correctly in the ledger.
